Roehampton Sports Ground Estate

Priory Lane and Bank Lane, London SW15 5JQ. Thirty-eight freehold acres owned by the Bank of England since 1908, home of the Wimbledon Qualifying Competition, offered as a whole or in four lots by Knight Frank. This brief sets out the estate, the income in place, the commercial business plan and the working underwrite for the BGP and Related partnership buying the whole estate together. The National Tennis Centre stays exactly as it is on the LTA's 125-year lease. The Grange and the cottages are valued at £7m on exit, BGP's valuation, with Related underwriting the residential conversion.

The AELTG step-up depends on the break.

Rent doubles to £675,000 on 1 August 2031. The tenant can walk away on 31 July 2031. In the current lease the uplift is only worth what the All England Club decides it is worth in 2031, which is the opening for a renegotiation now.

The business plan

Surrender and regrant, then the Third Space lease

Two legal steps make the plan, and both complete on the day we buy. The All England Club surrenders its 2021 lease of the whole Sports Centre and Grounds and takes a new 10-year lease of the playing fields, keeping the temporary pavilion and the squash courts for the Qualifying. The agreement for lease with Third Space exchanges at the same time. The landlord then strips the Sports Club and the whole permanent Pavilion back to a developer's shell, forms the new ground-floor link between them and renews the roofs and glazing for a 20-year lease, about three months' work, and the lease of the buildings and the astro pitch, 60,142 sq ft GIA, completes on handover with the capital contribution paid then. The Grange is held for a residential conversion, which Related are underwriting. The cottages sit with The Grange in the residential lot Related are underwriting. Lot 1 is not part of the plan: the National Tennis Centre remains the National Tennis Centre, the LTA keeps its lease to 2129 and no surrender or variation is proposed.

Move 1

Surrender and regrant with the All England Club

£100,000 pa

The Club surrenders its lease of the whole of Lot 2, which runs to 2036 with a 2031 break, and takes a new 10-year lease of the playing fields, the hard courts, the long-standing temporary pavilion at the north end of the Pavilion and the Squash Courts building, with the marquee rights already consented to 2031 and a break it can exercise once the Qualifying has moved to Wimbledon Park. The Pavilion, sports hall, pool and car parks come back to the landlord on the day of the surrender. The full proposal to the Club is in the Proposals section.

The Club's lease is outside the Act and runs to 2036, so the surrender has to be agreed, not imposed. Their lever is the 2031 break; ours is certainty of tenure for the Qualifying until Wimbledon Park is ready, a rent that falls from £350,000 to £100,000, the hospitality option in the Pavilion and a reopened pool that ends the local campaign. Document the surrender and regrant as a condition of the purchase so the leisure buildings are vacant on completion.

Move 2

Let the Sports Club and the whole Pavilion to Third Space

£1.80m pa

The Sports Club and the whole permanent Pavilion, 60,142 sq ft GIA; the 4,778 sq ft temporary pavilion, its link passage and porch stay with the Club outside the demise, severed from the Pavilion by the landlord's works. A 20-year lease at £30 per sq ft GIA with one year rent free and a capital contribution equal to one year's rent. Rent indexed to CPI, reviewed five-yearly, capped at 3 percent a year. The Squash Courts, 3,233 sq ft, are a separate building and are excluded from the demise; the fenced 2G astro pitch beside the car park goes in, with a five-metre strip around it for seating and access, and the 162 parking bays come as rights rather than demise. Their own brief was about 50,000 sq ft, so the area is a live input in the underwrite below. The heads of terms are in the Proposals section.

Two long-term routes, both existing

Residents and the grounds through the barrier, Third Space through the timber gates

Gate 1, the barrier: residents and the grounds. The barrier-controlled entrance off Bank Lane beside the cottage, immediately south-west of The Grange. The drive runs up past the sub-station to The Grange's forecourt and the road along its west side, so residents reach their 36 bays without touching the main car park, and the Club's groundsmen and event traffic reach the fields the same way under the traffic plan. Gate 2, the timber gates, Third Space. Forty metres further east along Bank Lane, a pair of timber gates opens straight into car park A. Today the car park runs one way, in at the barrier and out through these gates, which is where its painted EXIT arrows point; for Third Space the gates become the two-way entrance to their 162 bays and members walk up the road beside The Grange to the Sports Club's west door. Both gates exist and are in use, so swapping which traffic uses which is not development, provided neither is widened. The only other vehicle access to the estate is the Tennis Centre's own entrance off Priory Lane inside the LTA lease, which is not relied on.

Third Space's own door. The Sports Club already has its own entrance on its west elevation, facing the road that runs between The Grange and the club: a new entrance, canopy and ramps there were consented in 2004 (2004/2604) and again with the spa extension in 2007 (2007/3262). Members walk from car park A up that road and straight into the pool and hall building. With the whole Pavilion in the demise, Third Space also get the Pavilion's own front door. Nothing new needs building or consenting.

How the areas were measured.

The green GIA outlines were extracted from the Principal Plans PDFs and reproduce the schedule to within 0.1 sq m on every sheet; Knight Frank's building totals match. The temporary pavilion was measured along its own thin-walled outline on the ground-floor plan, so the hall's south-west corner stays in the demise. Principal Plans should confirm from the CAD before pricing, but these are measured figures, not estimates. The underwrite below uses 60,142 sq ft and can be changed.

Planning and risk

Buying without planning risk

The test for every part of the plan is that it works on existing consents, existing use classes and existing hardstanding, with nothing that needs a planning permission to make the numbers work. The table shows where each element stands. The one element that still needs a consent is The Grange conversion. Class MA prior approval is a 56-day, limited-test process, not a planning application, and the Bank is submitting it; the answer is sequencing, with the prior approval in hand before exchange or exchange conditional on it.

ElementPlanning positionStatusHow to keep it risk-free

Internal works are not development. The spa, sauna, creche and pool alterations were consented in 2007 and 2011 and are built.ExistingKeep the works inside the existing envelope. The Grange: Class MA summary

What the residential permitted development route needs

The brochure says a detailed planning summary and the technical documents for the PD application are in the Knight Frank data room. They were not in the files we received, and the Wandsworth planning history runs only to the March 2026 lawful development certificate for the grounds building, so the application has not been registered. Ask Knight Frank for the PD pack. Against the Class MA tests as they stand after the March 2024 changes:

  • Class E use for two years before the application. Offices since at least 2017, when the ground floor South Wing changed from leisure to office. Met.
  • Vacancy. The three-month vacancy test was removed in 2024. The ITF leases end 31 December 2026 in any case.
  • Floorspace cap. The 1,500 sq m limit was removed in 2024, so the whole 5,361 sq m can convert.
  • Exclusions. Not listed, not in a Conservation Area, not a scheduled monument or safety hazard area. Metropolitan Open Land is not an exclusion from Class MA.
  • Prior approval matters. Transport and highways, contamination, flooding, noise from commercial neighbours, natural light to every habitable room, fire safety where the building is 18 m or more, and adequate space standards. The transport test is where the 30 existing spaces and the shared car park come in.
  • Grounds building and courts. Nothing in Class MA allows external works, so balconies, new openings or a roof extension would need a full application on MOL. Related's scheme should assume conversion within the envelope.
Risk register
High

The surrender itself. The Club's lease runs to 2036 outside the Act, so the surrender and regrant must be signed up before exchange, with the new lease excluding the leisure buildings and both car parks. Without it, Move 2 cannot start until 2031 or 2036.

High

Condition of the leisure buildings. The Lighthouse vendor's survey annexed to the Club's lease (inspected August 2019, report 23 August 2020) put the immediate to short-term backlog at £13.85m across the estate at 2019 prices: Pavilion £4.18m (£2.5m roofs, windows, cladding and fabric; £1.68m M&E), Sports hall and pool £4.67m (£3.0m fabric including concrete carbonation; £1.67m M&E), squash courts £0.48m, The Grange £3.8m, cottages £0.42m, externals £0.3m. The Club's lease excused them from all of it. The appraisal carries the fabric items on the two leisure buildings as landlord's works at £130 per sq ft and leaves the M&E to Third Space's fit-out funded by the capital contribution; The Grange's £3.8m sits in Related's underwrite. A QS and an M&E engineer should price this before the bid is fixed.

High

Third Space covenant and terms. A 20-year lease on 60,142 sq ft at £30 GIA with three years of incentives is the whole commercial value, and is more space than the 50,000 sq ft they first asked for; the Squash Courts are the swing. Covenant strength, guarantor and the works specification need agreeing before the bid.

High

Grange prior approval. The conversion depends on Class MA prior approval, not yet applied for. Make it a condition of exchange or wait for the Bank's grant; the 56-day determination fits the timetable to a January 2027 completion.

Medium

Community campaign and Asset of Community Value. The Bank of England Centre Members' Group (saveboe.org) has campaigned since 2019 to keep the Sports Centre and pool for the community, with MPs Fleur Anderson and Sarah Olney and Sport England drawn in over the pool. Wandsworth's register shows the playing fields (football, rugby, cricket and the artificial pitch, not the buildings) listed as an Asset of Community Value on 1 August 2019 on a Roehampton and Putney Heath nomination; the Bank gave notice of disposal that September, the community moratorium ran to March 2020 and the listing expired in 2024. A fresh nomination can be made at any time and would put a six-month moratorium on the sale, so check the register at exchange. Expect the Third Space plan to be judged locally on whether the pool and hall stay open to local members, which is also the Club's interest.

Medium

Parking. 198 marked bays traced from the 2019 survey against 180 needed. Car park A was never in the Club's 2021 lease, which excludes it with The Grange, so nothing has to come back; the LTA holds a 2008 licence over 30 of its spaces at £18,000 a year, terminable on two months' notice, which the partnership inherits and can end.

Medium

Value of The Grange and cottages. Taken at BGP's £7m exit valuation, realised with everything else at the end of year 3; no holding or conversion cost is charged against it here, since both sit in Related's residential underwrite. Every £1m on that value moves profit on cost by about 4 points at the £18m base case.

Medium

Guarantor on the Tennis Centre lease. Due diligence only; the LTA lease is not being touched. The 2011 deed substituted LTA CLG Ltd for the All England Club. Confirm the brochure's "Lawn Tennis Association Limited" is the same entity, and that nothing has changed since.

Low

Title. Rent-charges of £57 from a 1779 deed on titles 239100 and 396768; Registrar's restrictions against charges on the older titles; a 1997 sub-station lease and 2009 EDF transformer lease; a right of way over part of Clarence House. Nothing seen that blocks the plan.

Low

VAT. Brochure says The Grange is opted to tax; Gerald Eve's 2025 budget says the landlord has not waived exemption. Reconcile before structuring.

Note

Environmental. Groundsure Siteguard (September 2019) concluded acceptable environmental risk for banking security; Part 2A or third-party action unlikely.

Planning history
  • Metropolitan Open Land across the whole estate. Not listed, not in a Conservation Area. The Wandsworth Local Plan 2023-2038 (partial review 2026) and the London Plan 2021 apply. Policy LP54 strongly resists loss of sports pitches, playing fields, indoor sports facilities and land last used for outdoor sport.
  • Wimbledon Qualifying consents: 2025/4672 approved January 2026 for marquees and temporary facilities for five years; 2024/0088 for marquees and grandstands; a 2023 amendment to add grandstands was refused and later consented properly. 2025/2066 approved a new grounds maintenance building; 2026/1109 a lawful development certificate for its construction compound.
  • Sports Centre: 2004/2604 new west entrance with canopy and ramps and veranda infill; 2004/5058 two floodlit hard courts; 2007/3262 sauna, steam room and spa extension and new west entrance and canopy to the sports hall and pool building; 2008/4309 medical clinic in the pool building; 2011/5340 creche extension to the clubhouse; 2011/3582 storage building.
  • The Grange: 2005/5242 access ramp; 2017/2937 ground floor South Wing from leisure to office.
  • National Tennis Centre consent 2003/2964, with an Environmental Statement, provided the replacement courts and pitches for the Bank's sports club; 2009/0937 seasonal canopy over two clay courts.
Documents

Everything received from the Knight Frank data room on 16 October 2026, filed in the BGP repository under technical/roehampton-sports-ground-estate. Links open on GitHub and need access to the repository; ask BGP for a copy otherwise. Missing from the pack so far: the All England Club's lease of Lot 2 and the EPCs.
